_doc: l23_whatchanged_language.json — the rule table for cure_l23_whatchanged_language.py.
_why: intel_2026.whatChanged is rendered to clients at apps/mouth/src/app/kbli/[code]/page.tsx:689
(and :428 for the gold copy). It is composed by concatenating the record's `mapping_note`
VERBATIM onto an English lead sentence — and mapping_note is Italian machine output from the
crosswalk pipeline. The result is an English regulatory page whose 2025-transition section
speaks Italian. Measured on origin/main 2026-07-26: 346 of 1,559 records (22.2%) contain at
least one of the literal templates below. Proven live on prod before this cure:
/kbli/46442 -> 'Il KBLI 2025 mantiene 46442 separato da 46441, rafforzando la distinzione...'
_scope_and_its_limit: This cure is DETERMINISTIC and covers the six template classes only. It is NOT a claim that
whatChanged is now entirely English. A residue of free-prose Italian exists that matches no
template (e.g. 46442's hand-written 'Il KBLI 2025 mantiene ... rafforzando la distinzione
regolatorio-ministeriale ...'); the compiler COUNTS and PRINTS that residue every run rather
than letting it pass as covered. Reporting a bound, not a truth: 346 is a FLOOR derived from
literal matching; a looser word-list matcher scored ~353, and a looser matcher can also score
false positives. Never cite either number as 'the number of Italian records'.
Same discipline the corner already records for the tier-claim matcher (19 <= truth <= 152).
_the_trap_guarded_here: One record carries an ENGLISH audit note that QUOTES the Italian label as history:
"Corrected 2026-07-19 - the previous 'match con aggregazione' status_mapping/label was stale".
A bare phrase replacement would rewrite that citation and corrupt an audit trail. Every rule
below is therefore anchored on its full template context ('KBLI 2020->2025 mapping: ' prefix,
or a 5-digit code operand) so it CANNOT fire inside a quoted historical label. The innocence
corpus pins this: superscar #3 says match the entity, never the bare substring.

rules.note: 181 records. Anchored on the 'mapping: ' prefix so a quoted label is untouched.
133 records. The 'mapping: ' anchor is what protects the 2026-07-19 audit citation.
9 records. The code operand keeps the match anchored to the real template.
16 records. Reached as 'Aggregation: Dati da ...' — the lead word is already English.

rules.pattern: Verifica e aggiornamento (NIB|OSS) (?:ora richiesti|da eseguire ora) dopo la chiusura della finestra di giugno (\d{4})\.
rules.replacement: \1 verification and update are now required following the closure of the June \2 window.
rules.note: 7 records across 4 wordings. Both Italian variants ('ora richiesti' / 'da eseguire ora') carry the same obligation, so they render to one English sentence.

A RAW ENUM leaking onto a public page — the same disease as L1.1 (raw-enum leak in 'By the numbers'), recurring on a different field. Source: build_what_changed's fallback branch, kbli_enrichment_pipeline.py:351 — `STATUS_MAP.get(mapping, f"Mapping status: {mapping}.")` prints the identifier verbatim whenever the status is not in STATUS_MAP. Here the enum trails an already-English sentence ('Direct match from KBLI 2020 (MATCH_LANGSUNG).'), so the cure simply DROPS the parenthetical and the sentence stands. The four tokens are enumerated literally, never matched as an ALL-CAPS shape: NIB / OSS / KBLI / PMA are legitimate acronyms on these pages and a shape-matcher would eat them.

The same leak in leading position ('MATCH_LANGSUNG — direct match from KBLI 2020.'). Dropping the token would leave the sentence starting lowercase, so the first letter of the surviving clause is re-capitalised — see uppercase_first_group in the compiler for why that is a per-rule flag and not a blanket post-pass.

8 occurrences of the parenthetical carrying a trailing word: "it didn't exist in 2020 (BPS_ONLY status)." The first parenthetical rule requires the parens to hold ONLY the token, so this variant slipped it — found by re-running the residue probe after that rule landed, which is the point of having a probe that does not reuse the cure's own rules.
'CODICE_RINUMERATO from KBLI 2020 code 62012.' — leading token followed by 'from', not an em-dash. The English participle matches STATUS_MAP's own verb for this status.
Same shape for the aggregation status.
'The MATCH_CON_AGGREGAZIONE mapping means some activities...' — the token used as an adjective mid-sentence. Lower-case replacement because the article before it already carries the capital.

The bare form, where the enum IS the whole sentence and there is no English left to keep. The replacement is NOT authored here: it is STATUS_MAP['MATCH_LANGSUNG'] verbatim from kbli_enrichment_pipeline.py:96 — the pipeline author's own rendering of this exact status. Ordered AFTER the parenthetical/dash rules so it only ever sees what they left.

rules.replacement: Renumbered from KBLI 2020. Your OSS registration may need updating to the new code.
rules.note: STATUS_MAP['CODICE_RINUMERATO'] verbatim (kbli_enrichment_pipeline.py:97).

rules.replacement: This code consolidates multiple KBLI 2020 activities into one. Verify your specific activity maps correctly.
rules.note: STATUS_MAP['MATCH_CON_AGGREGAZIONE'] verbatim (kbli_enrichment_pipeline.py:98).

rules.replacement: New in KBLI 2025 — no equivalent in KBLI 2020. Register fresh on OSS.
rules.note: STATUS_MAP['BPS_ONLY'] verbatim (kbli_enrichment_pipeline.py:99).

3 gold records. The leading-token rule required the literal 'from KBLI'; here the token is followed straight by a bare code ('CODICE_RINUMERATO from 68130'). An UNDER-match I introduced by anchoring on the wrong side of the operand — found by the residue probe on the SECOND surface, which is why gold is scanned and not assumed to mirror canonical.

rules.replacement: new in KBLI 2025, with PP28 data
rules.note: 4 gold records: 'New code in KBLI 2025 (BPS_ONLY with PP28 data).' The parenthetical carries real information (PP28 data exists) so it is rendered, not dropped.
The token used as a noun-adjective: 'This is a BPS_ONLY code — it exists in...'.
'maintains the classification as BPS_ONLY, meaning...' — same token, adverbial position.

9 records. DELETED, not translated — deliberately. This is internal pipeline bookkeeping about a code the cleaner dropped; it is not information a client can act on, and it was never meant to reach a public page. The fact itself is not lost: which 2020 codes a record does and does not carry is recorded structurally in the crosswalk fields (pp28_sources / kbli_2020_source), which is where an audit trail belongs. This is the one rule that removes rather than renders, and it is called out here so the removal is a recorded decision rather than a silent side effect.
